summary: Verified and adapted the open upstream candidate from https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37458. Automatically selected TCPStore rendezvous ports now avoid Linux's ephemeral client-port range when possible and exclude ports planned for other SGLang listeners. Explicit --nccl-port values are unchanged.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before regression: collection failed because the non-ephemeral rendezvous allocator did not exist.
67 focused socket/PortArgs tests plus 4 subtests passed, including reported range 10000-61000, listener exclusions, full-range exhaustion, and missing-procfs fallback.

tests.command: /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-ae4788091d67/venv/bin/python TCPStore probe (64 bind(0) samples, 8 rendezvous selections, 8 concurrent world_size=1 TCPStores)
tests.what_was_measured: Host ephemeral range was 32768-60999; 64/64 ordinary bind(0) ports were inside it, 8/8 rendezvous ports were outside it, and all 8 real PyTorch TCPStore servers bound concurrently.
Changed Python sources compile and the patch has no whitespace errors.
252 passed and 2 unrelated existing ROCm context-parallel tests failed because HIP rejects deprecated prefill CP before their expected validation point.

remaining_limitations: The reported 8x NVIDIA H800 hardware and Qwen3-Embedding weights were unavailable, so the full model-serving workload was not reproduced.
Only one gfx950 GPU was assigned, so this does not claim an 8-GPU or architecture-equivalent reproduction.

The assigned AMD Instinct MI355X gfx950 was visible through Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2, but no GPU kernels were executed because the defect and deterministic checks are CPU TCP socket/TCPStore startup behavior.
The original failure is intermittent. Evidence validates its concrete port-allocation mechanism and real TCPStore binding, not its production frequency.
The related upstream fix remains an open candidate at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37458.
